description: B7 matrix-valued inverse problem: identify the order alpha and two rates of the GKSL generator of the driven two-level system from noisy partial observations of rho, D^alpha rho = L[rho] on tau in [0,1]
identifiability: the solution is invariant under (tau_c, L) -> (s tau_c, s^(alpha-1) L); tau_c is therefore fixed (tau_c = T_r, the length of the time window) and the Rabi frequency Omega is known, so that alpha and the two rates in units of 1/T_r are identifiable; what the data determine in general is alpha and the products tau_c^(1-alpha) T_r^alpha * rate

xz.note: pure initial state; <sigma_x> and <sigma_z> are measured, <sigma_y> is not

pop.note: populations only (rho_ee), pure excited initial state; the dephasing rate is weakly identifiable

obs_times: sorted uniform sample of [0.02, 1], the same for all realisations
seeds: realisation k: data noise from default_rng(2000 + k), initial guesses from default_rng(3000 + k), network seed k

pinn.parametrisation: alpha = 0.05 + 0.95 sigmoid(a), rates = exp(u); the current alpha is used in the L1 weights and in the gate

pilot.selection: per (design, noise level): the weight with the smallest median over the pilot realisations of the root-mean-square relative parameter error; the selected weight is used for all maps

N128_interp.note: the mesh of the networks, piecewise-linear interpolation to the observation times

N128.note: the graded mesh with the observation times added as nodes

N512.note: refined mesh: the L1 error is about (1/4)^(2 - alpha) of that at N = 128

nls.projection: optional: noisy data projected on the admissible set before the fit (xz: the pair (sx, sz) on the unit disc; pop: the population on [0, 1])

crb.note: Cramer-Rao bound from the Jacobian of the L1 solution (N = 2048, observation times as nodes) at the true parameters
